metadata.title: Density Pass 31 -- Wright's Almost-Breakthrough on Cemetery Ridge (Ticks 308-320)
metadata.description: Ambrose Wright's Georgia brigade crests Cemetery Ridge, briefly reaches the crest, and almost breaks the Union army in two — before being driven back unsupported. Wright later said he had pierced the Union line but had no support. The moment that came closest to Confederate victory on July 2, less famous than the Little Round Top fight but arguably more dangerous.

placements.notes: Wright's Georgia brigade -- Anderson's division. About to make the most dangerous Confederate attack of July 2.
Posey's Mississippi brigade -- supposed to support Wright's left. Will not advance far enough.
Mahone's Virginia brigade -- supposed to support Wright's right. Will also not advance.
Webb's brigade on Cemetery Ridge -- holding the Union center
Harrow's brigade -- the men who will face Pickett tomorrow
Wright CHARGING across the Emmitsburg Road -- driving everything before him
Webb's brigade falling back -- Wright is pushing through the Union line
Wright AT THE CREST of Cemetery Ridge -- he can see the Baltimore Pike below. The army is cut in two.
Brown's Rhode Island battery -- Wright is at the guns. The gunners are fighting hand-to-hand.
Posey stalled short of the Emmitsburg Road -- Wright's left is naked
Mahone not advancing -- Wright's right is also naked
Caldwell's division countercharging -- Hancock has sent every man he has
Gibbon's remaining brigades hitting Wright's flank
Wright REPULSED -- unsupported on the crest, hit from three sides. He will say: We were on the crest -- we had the victory in our grasp.
Webb's brigade back on the ridge -- the crest held. But for 10 minutes the Union army was cut in two.
Wright's survivors reforming -- 754 casualties. The most dangerous moment on July 2 that no one remembers.
